question: Should OpenClaw publish an OpenAPI contract for Gateway programmatic access, and should it cover only documented HTTP routes or also attempt to model WebSocket RPC/protocol schemas?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing schema scope defines a supported API/discovery contract across security-sensitive Gateway HTTP routes, TypeBox protocol schemas, and the client SDK direction.

options.title: Approve HTTP-only OpenAPI
options.body: Generate and publish a versioned OpenAPI document for documented HTTP routes with explicit auth semantics while leaving WebSocket RPC on TypeBox/JSON Schema.

options.title: Defer to TypeBox and SDK
options.body: Keep the existing protocol JSON Schema and Gateway client/app SDK surfaces as the supported programmatic path until maintainers want an HTTP OpenAPI contract.

options.title: Serve Runtime Schema
options.body: Expose /openapi.json or Swagger UI from the Gateway only after deciding route inclusion, auth requirements, and private-ingress behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve HTTP-only OpenAPI
recommendation.body: Generate and publish a versioned OpenAPI document for documented HTTP routes with explicit auth semantics while leaving WebSocket RPC on TypeBox/JSON Schema.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across Gateway protocol docs, schema/client-package direction, and adjacent Gateway API maintenance.
